To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) TGase 2 depletes I-kappaBα in cells, but the polymers formed are not detected in cells; 2) mu-calpain and the ubiquitin proteasome pathway contribute in parallel to the degradation of TGase 1-induced I-kappaB alpha polymers; 3) inhibition of both calpain and the ubiquitine proteasome pathway results in the accumulation of I kappaB alpha polymers and I kappaB alpha in cells.

(1) the combined inhibition of mu-calpain and the proteosome leads to an increased accumulation of I-kapaBalpha polymers, and I-kappa Balpha, concurrent with the inhibition of NF-kB activity in MCF7 and MDA-MB 231 breast cancer cells.

TGase 2 depletion of I-kBalpha occurs in parallel with proteasome degradation, and that mu-calpain inhibition can block the degradation of I-kB polymers, leading to the accumulation of both I-B and I-B polymers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of NF-kappa activation and I-kappa depletion in cells over-expressing TGase2.
the mechanism of I-kappaBa degradation in the presence of TGase  2.
the role of TGase 1 and TGase 2 in NF-kappaB regulation, which may provide new insights for the development of therapeutic approaches against drug-resistant cancers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the depletion of I-kappabeta by TGase 2 and calpain is a mechanism that occurs in parallel with ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation.

the I-kappaB alpha depletion by transgluatinase 2 and calpain proteolysis occurs in parallel with ubiquitin-proteosoma pathway and that the calpain and proteasome inhibition results in an accumulation of both I kappaB alpha polymers and I kappaB alpha, concurrent with an NF-kappa B inhibition.
the depletion of I-kapaBalpha by TGase2 and mu-calpains occurs in parallel with ubiquitin-protease pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the depletion of free I-kappa B by transglutamine 2 and calpain in the presence of proteasome occurs in parallel, and the inhibition of proteasome or calpain can lead to an increased accumulation of the polymer and free I-kappa-B, respectively.
the I-kappaB-alpha depletion by TGase2 is mediated by calpain and ubiquitin-proteosome pathway in parallel, which may be a new mechanism of NF-kappa-B activation.
I-kappaB alpha is a substrate for TG2 and calpain and that these enzymes may act in concert to regulate I-kappaB-alpha degradation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the I-kappaB polymers are not stable in cells and can be degraded in a parallel pathway to the ubiquitin proteasome pathway.

TGase 2-mediated depletion of I kappa B alpha occurs through the calpain system and the ubiquitin-protesome pathway, and the combined inhibition of the calpain and the ubiquitin proteasome pathways may be a novel approach for cancer therapy.
the I-kappaB polymers can be metabolized via calpain, which is an alternative pathway to proteasome.
